name: Kalshi
description: US event-contract exchange and one of the two best-known prediction-market venues. During TOKEN2049 week, John Wang (Head of Crypto) speaks twice on the official programme, and Kalshi co-hosts evenings with Haruko and Insilico. Its full order-book data streams over DoubleZero, and ION and Coinbase support clearing and settlement of its event contracts. Kalshi Klear has been reported as requesting institutional margining; that is a request, not an approval. Internationally, Kalshi has begun expanding through brokerage partners (XP in Brazil; Alpaca’s infrastructure), which makes Asia-based distribution a live question.

name: Polymarket
description: Prediction-market platform and one of the two best-known venues. Its founder headlines a main-stage fireside, and it hosts its first Singapore kick-off event on Wednesday evening. FT reporting says Polymarket is pushing for financial-product treatment in the UK/EU; regulators' positions are contested. In Singapore specifically, the Gambling Regulatory Authority declared Polymarket an unlicensed gambling site and ordered it blocked in January 2025.

name: Hyperliquid
description: Onchain trading venue. Its HIP-4 upgrade lets third-party builders deploy outcome markets permissionlessly, with shared-margin mechanics. Hosts an ecosystem event on Monday and is the focus of the Hyperliquid Forum on Tuesday; Jeff Yan speaks on the main stage.

name: Predict.fun
description: Prediction-market platform and TOKEN2049 Gold sponsor. It has announced Chainlink-based market lifecycle and settlement, and block trading of 100,000+ shares with liquidity from Susquehanna Crypto (company claims).

name: Outcome / Outcome Labs
description: Builder in the Hyperliquid outcome-market ecosystem. Ahmed Salih (Outcome Labs) and Jack Booth (Outcome) are listed for the Hyperliquid Forum.

name: Predict365
description: Prediction-market product. It has publicly said its team will be at Marina Bay Sands on 7–8 October and is inviting meetings with people building in prediction markets, trading and fintech.

name: PowerScale
description: Consumer and social prediction-market product combining crypto, anime and social features. Hosts a free Thursday evening event.

name: Lighter
description: Represented by Vladimir Novakovski on “The Speculation Age” panel with Kalshi and Robinhood.

name: Robinhood
description: Brokerage. Its Robinhood Chain session and its seat on “The Speculation Age” panel speak to whether prediction markets end up as one asset inside mainstream trading apps.

name: Zoomex
description: Crypto trading platform hosting a Wednesday traders’ after-party whose panel covers derivatives, TradFi and prediction markets.

name: ChainUp
description: Enterprise crypto infrastructure provider and TOKEN2049 Gold sponsor (booth PB4-8). Sells Hermes, white-label prediction-market software with shared-liquidity claims that have not been independently tested. Hosts the Institutional Ark evening on Tuesday.

name: DoubleZero
description: Specialised low-latency network. Kalshi streams full order books over DoubleZero, and it has expanded the categories of Kalshi data it carries. Founder Austin Federa gives a Thursday keynote.

name: Kaiko
description: Digital-asset market-data provider and co-host of Wednesday's Opening Bell institutional breakfast. Adjacent to the prediction-market data layer.

name: Chainlink
description: Oracle and data infrastructure. Predict.fun has adopted Chainlink for market lifecycle and settlement. Listed as a HypurrCo partner and a Finality Forum participant. Andrew McCormick (Chainlink) is on Wednesday’s tokenised-markets panel.

name: ION
description: Financial-markets infrastructure firm that partnered with Coinbase to support Kalshi event contracts, covering clearing, reporting, resolution and settlement.
note: No TOKEN2049-week appearance recorded; included for the stack.

name: Haruko
description: Institutional portfolio and risk platform with Kalshi and Polymarket integrations. Co-hosts Monday's invite-only gathering with Kalshi. The integrations are documented; actual institutional usage is not.

name: Insilico Terminal
description: Trading terminal and execution tooling. Co-hosts the Kalshi x Insilico Asia Session for active traders on Thursday, and is listed as a HypurrCo partner.

name: Nansen
description: Listed as a partner of HypurrCo Gathers.

name: Tread.fi
description: Listed as a partner of HypurrCo Gathers.

name: Wintermute
description: Market maker that has publicly entered prediction markets as a two-sided liquidity provider. It has separately argued that the category has infrastructure weaknesses around thin books, fees and APIs (company opinion). Listed as a HypurrCo partner and a Finality Forum participant.

name: Susquehanna Crypto
description: Named by Predict.fun as the liquidity provider behind its block-trading service (company claim).

It is also listed at the Finality Forum. Not a prediction-market company, but exactly the kind of liquidity firm prediction-market traders should know is in town.

name: PredictBay

By its own disclosure, paper trading is the live product today and the DeepBook Predict integration is on testnet. Its CMO Zack Nelson speaks at Sui Basecamp on Thursday 8 October, and the company ties its TOKEN-week appearance to its planned $PBAY token.
